exposure: Hanging pannus vs no hanging pannus
cohort: Patients with BMI ≥ 50 kg/m(2) undergoing cesarean delivery at a single center from 2016 to 2020
finding: In patients with super obesity and hanging pannus, supraumbilical vertical midline incision was not significantly different from Pfannenstiel's incision in terms of composite outcome of blood transfusion need and surgical complications, but was associated with increased risk of classical hysterotomy and blood loss.
mod_finding: Supraumbilical vertical midline incision was associated with a higher likelihood of classical hysterotomy compared to Pfannenstiel's incision.
